annotations.description: Player timed out or passed on the mandatory discard from Slate Street Ruffian's trigger, losing control over which card to discard. The game auto-selected a card, which may not have been optimal. With Blood Artist and Vito on board, Eternal Thirst is extremely valuable (lifelink + Vito doubles life drain), and Last Gasp is premium removal. Ronom Unicorn would likely be the correct discard as it's the least impactful card in this board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Failed to respond to the discard trigger, letting the game auto-select a card to discard.
annotations.betterLine: Actively choose to discard Ronom Unicorn, as it's the least synergistic card with the Blood Artist/Vito engine, preserving Last Gasp (removal), Eternal Thirst (lifelink synergy with Vito), and Inspiring Unicorn (board presence).

annotations.description: Blood Artist's trigger was targeted at themselves instead of the opponent. With Vito on the battlefield, targeting the opponent would cause: opponent loses 1 (Blood Artist) + gain 1 life (Blood Artist) triggering Vito for another 1 damage to opponent = opponent loses 2, you gain 1. By targeting themselves, they lose 1 and gain 1 (net 0) but Vito still triggers for 1 to opponent. This is a 3-point life swing difference (from +2 net to -1 net for themselves).
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Blood Artist's trigger, losing 1 life and gaining 1 life.
annotations.betterLine: Target MstLg Perfect with Blood Artist's trigger to make the opponent lose 1 life while gaining 1 life, which also triggers Vito for an additional 1 damage to the opponent.

annotations.description: Blood Artist's trigger targets a player who loses 1 life, and the controller gains 1 life regardless. With Vito on the battlefield, the life gain triggers Vito to deal 1 to the opponent. By targeting themselves, the net result is: self loses 1, self gains 1 (net 0), opponent loses 1 (from Vito). By targeting the opponent, the result would be: self gains 1, opponent loses 1 (from Blood Artist) + 1 (from Vito) = 2. Targeting themselves costs 1 damage to the opponent for no benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Blood Artist's trigger
annotations.betterLine: Target MstLg Perfect (the opponent) with Blood Artist's trigger to deal 2 total damage to the opponent (1 from Blood Artist + 1 from Vito) instead of just 1

annotations.description: At 8 life facing multiple attackers, casting Inspiring Unicorn for 4 mana taps out completely, leaving no interaction available. The opponent has 5-7 potential damage on board next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Inspiring Unicorn for 2WW, using all available mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ronom Unicorn for 1W, leaving 1B open (with Thriving Moor) to hold up Last Gasp as instant-speed removal during opponent's combat. This provides a blocker while keeping interaction available to survive at 8 life.

annotations.description: Casting Inspired Charge precombat main phase instead of during combat (after attackers/blocks declared) reveals the pump unnecessarily. More importantly, at 3 life with Keldon Raider 4/3 about to untap, spending all mana on offense instead of playing Ronom Unicorn (extra body) and holding Last Gasp mana for defense against the 4/3 is risky. The 3 extra damage (12 vs 9) may not justify losing the ability to kill Keldon Raider on opponent's turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Inspired Charge for 2WW in precombat main, spending all mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ronom Unicorn (1W), attack with all four creatures for ~9 damage with Inspiring Unicorn trigger, keep 1B+1 open for Last Gasp to handle Keldon Raider 4/3 on opponent's turn

annotations.description: Blood Artist's trigger was targeted at themselves instead of the opponent. In a tight race (4 life vs 6 life), this wastes the 1 life loss that should go to the opponent. With Vito on board, targeting the opponent would result in: opponent loses 1 (to 5), gain 1 life, Vito triggers for another 1 damage (opponent to 4). Instead, targeting self means: lose 1 then gain 1 (net zero), Vito triggers for 1 (opponent to 5). This is a 2-point swing in effective damage in a very close game.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Blood Artist's 'target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life' trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Target MstLg Perfect (the opponent) with Blood Artist's trigger to deal 1 life loss to opponent and gain 1 life, which also triggers Vito for an additional 1 damage to opponent.
